page.layout: One page of text, with running head and page number at top; two numbered-figure diagrams of division proofs set in the text block, one after the first paragraph and one after the second. No margin notes.

main_text.head: Probatio Divisionis.
main_text.p: Si autem scire cupio an recte primum exemplum diviserim, abjicio 9 a quoto in semicirculo, & 5 remanent, quae ad dextrum latus literæ X colloco, & Divisorem, nempe 3 ad sinistrum latus scribo, dices: Ter 5. sunt 15, 5 & 1 sunt 6, q; supra X noto. Deinde abjicio 9 a Dividendo, & remanent 6, q; sub X noto.
main_text.l: [Division proof diagram: the cross-multiplication scheme of the first example, with the numbers (18104 and the quotient 3, 6, 5, 6 arranged around an X-shaped cross]
main_text.p: Exemplum cum duobus Divisoribus sic probo: Abjicio 9 a Quoto, & 2 quae remanent, ad dextrum latus literæ X noto, & Divisores per additionē conjungo, dicens: 1 & 2 sunt 3, ter bina vel bis terna sunt 6, quibus residuum, nempe 3 addo, & sunt 9: Et scribo o supra X. Deinde abjicio 9 a Dividendo, & remanet o, quam sub X colloco. Sed huic Regulæ non nimiū confidendum; quia, ut nonnulli experti sunt, sæpè fallit.
main_text.l: [Division proof diagram: the cross-multiplication scheme of the second example, with the numbers (3 and (470 and the quotient 3, 2, 0 arranged around an X-shaped cross]

page.notes: The two worked division proofs are diagrams of casting-out-nines calculations with small symbols (crosses, dots, circles) that cannot be fully reproduced as text; the diagram lines are descriptions, not transcription. The printed numerals in the diagrams are (18104 and (470, with quotient digits 3,6,5,6 and 3,2,0 respectively. The "q;" forms are printed abbreviations for -que and are kept as printed. "nimiū" is printed with a macron over u. Long s is rendered as s throughout.
